subject.title: feature: system event priority/bypass-queue mode for reliable in-session alerts

question: Should OpenClaw add a privileged high-priority system-event path, and should it bypass heartbeat/session lanes or use a typed operator notification surface instead?
rationale: The requested behavior changes trusted alert delivery, prompt-visible system-message ordering, busy-lane protection, and abuse controls, so automation cannot choose the permanent contract safely.

options.title: Design priority alert contract
options.body: Add an explicit, authenticated high-priority alert path with sanitization, rate/flood limits, transcript-ordering rules, and busy-lane tests.

options.title: Use notification surface
options.body: Make connected-UI/admin notifications the canonical urgent-alert path and keep prompt-visible system events heartbeat-mediated.

options.title: Keep best-effort semantics
options.body: Document that in-session system events can be delayed under saturated lanes and rely on external channels for outage alerts.

recommendation.title: Design priority alert contract
recommendation.body: Add an explicit, authenticated high-priority alert path with sanitization, rate/flood limits, transcript-ordering rules, and busy-lane tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans CLI, Gateway wake behavior, heartbeat scheduling, system-event security, and UI alert product semantics where this account has the strongest history signal.
